walkthroughs.body_html:
Area of Study 2: Vocal Music — a core area of GCSE Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Area of Study 2: Vocal Music brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Area of Study 2: Vocal Music.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the function of the bridge in a pop song?
options: Entirely new material is introduced.
It is the very first section.
It is the same as the chorus.
To provide contrast before the final chorus, often by changing melody, key, or texture.

mcqs.q: What happens in the recapitulation of sonata form?
options: ii to V.
Entirely new material is introduced.
The exposition is repeated exactly.
Both subjects return, but the second subject is now in the tonic key.

mcqs.q: Which chords form a plagal cadence?
options: IV to I (the 'amen' cadence).
ii to V.
It is the very first section.
V to I.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Soprano”?
options: High male voice; range roughly C3-C5.
Lowest male voice; range roughly E2-E4.
Highest female voice; range roughly C4-A5.
Low female voice; range roughly F3-F5.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Tenor”?
options: Lowest male voice; range roughly E2-E4.
Vocal performance without instrumental accompaniment.
High male voice; range roughly C3-C5.
Highest female voice; range roughly C4-A5.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Falsetto”?
options: Vocal performance without instrumental accompaniment.
Low female voice; range roughly F3-F5.
Lowest male voice; range roughly E2-E4.
Male singing in a high register above the normal range, using cord-edge vibration.
